themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints exploded to 138 THIS WEEK—a 431% spike from the 26-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.36)—suggesting a sudden deterioration in road quality across Sunnyside/Woodside that warrants immediate investigation into cause and scope.
evidence: 138 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 26.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Complements ongoing CB budget requests for street/infrastructure investment
reporting_angles: Ground-truth reporting: drive/walk key neighborhoods to document specific street failures (potholes, cracking, subsidence)
City response: contact DDOT to understand whether a single weather event, deferred maintenance backlog, or contractor failure drove the spike

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Epidemic
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints surged to 5 last week—a stunning 3,900% spike from a 0.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 14.74)—suggesting a coordinated campaign or sudden enforcement gap for signage violations across the district.
evidence: 5 illegal posting complaints last week vs. 0.1 average over prior 8 weeks
3,900% increase with z-score of 14.74 (highest statistical anomaly in dataset)
Concentrated spike suggests localized campaign rather than chronic issue
reporting_angles: Visual survey: locate and photograph illegal postings; identify patterns (political, commercial, gang-related, construction)
Enforcement angle: why did complaints spike now? Did a business, developer, or political campaign trigger enforcement action?

themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Surge
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints jumped to 12 last week—a 284% increase from the 3.1 weekly average (z-score: 7.61)—coinciding with spikes in unsanitary conditions and animal complaints, suggesting an emerging pest control or waste management failure.
evidence: 12 rodent complaints last week vs. 3.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Correlated with spikes in unsanitary animal/private property complaints (3 last week vs. 0.1 avg) and street sweeping complaints (5 last week vs. 0.2 avg)
reporting_angles: Ground reporting: interview residents with complaints; document rodent sightings, droppings, burrowing in specific blocks
City response: contact DOHMH and Sanitation to understand whether a waste collection failure, building closure, or contractor withdrawal triggered the outbreak

themes_detail.label: Building Code Violations Spike
themes_detail.summary: Building/use complaints surged to 9 THIS WEEK—a 260% increase from the 2.5 weekly average (z-score: 4.91)—alongside 560 total DOB filings in the last 90 days, suggesting rapid development activity creating compliance or occupancy issues.
evidence: 9 building/use complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
560 DOB filings in last 90 days (378 alterations, 98 new buildings) suggest active construction ecosystem
reporting_angles: Development pressure: map active ULURP rezonings (21-31 46th Ave, 50-02 Queens Blvd, 31-10/31-16 Hunters Point Ave) to see if violations cluster near permitted sites
Compliance angle: interview DOB about whether rapid alteration filings are outpacing inspection capacity

themes_detail.label: Street Noise and Sweeping Failures
themes_detail.summary: Street/sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 32 last week (216% spike from 10.1 avg, z-score: 4.37) and street sweeping complaints hit 5 last week (1,900% spike from 0.2 avg, z-score: 10.97)—together suggesting sanitation service degradation or construction/demolition surge.
evidence: 32 street/sidewalk noise complaints last week vs. 10.1 weekly average (216% increase, z-score: 4.37)
5 street sweeping complaints last week vs. 0.2 weekly average (1,900% increase, z-score: 10.97)
Dual spike suggests systemic Sanitation Department service gap or external construction activity
reporting_angles: Sanitation response: contact NYC Sanitation to confirm whether staffing, equipment, or route changes triggered sweep complaint surge
Construction correlation: cross-reference complaints with DOB demolition/alteration filings to see if active sites are generating dust and noise
